paper.title: Algorithm 771: rksuite_90: Fortran 90 software for ordinary differential equation initial value problems
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 23(3), 402 (Sep 1997); netlib TOMS 771
paper.note: DOI not verified in this wake; the article was not read (paywalled). The claim rests on the shipped reference output eg_simple_c0_a.r inside the archive (the archive's own example set).

code.note: Fortran 90 shar archive. Unpack the shar (drop everything above the #! /bin/sh line, run with /bin/sh) into a fresh directory outside the site. Build the rksuite_90 module with the example eg_simple_c0_a.f90 using gfortran, run it, and compare its printed output with the shipped eg_simple_c0_a.r.

claim.location: The shipped reference output eg_simple_c0_a.r (archive member, example program eg_simple_c0_a.f90): the line 'The cost of the integration in calls to F was 117'. The paper was not read; no paper table or page is cited.
claim.metric: Number of calls to the user's derivative routine F made by RKSUITE_90 integrating the eg_simple_c0_a problem (integer count).
claim.paper_value: Not used: the TOMS article was not read; the value is the one in the shipped eg_simple_c0_a.r.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The count is an integer from an adaptive step-size scheme; a different floating-point rounding (compiler, optimisation level) can move it by a step or two, so +/-2 calls allows that and nothing more. Not to be loosened after any run.

claim.note: Chosen over the printed error estimates in eg_two_body.r, whose digits depend on rounding more directly. Its ymax and solution tables are not used because they are printed to 3-4 significant figures.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 5 minutes: gfortran compile of the rksuite_90 module and one small example.
cost.data_size: None; the example hard-codes its problem.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: A deterministic adaptive ODE solver whose shipped example prints an integer call count that depends on the step-size control actually running, not on a value derivable on paper.
